newsitem.title: UK: EUROTUNNEL ADDS UP FIRE COSTS.
newsitem.headline: EUROTUNNEL ADDS UP FIRE COSTS.

text.p: Debt-laden Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA said Wednesday revenues were back on track after last November's fire, with turnover so far this year running in line with forecasts in its huge loan restructuring plan.

Eurotunnel said service interruptions caused by the fire cut turnover to 168.8 million pounds ($266.5 million) in the first six months of 1997, from 223.6 million ($353 million) in the first half of 1996, but compensation received from its fire insurance added 52.4 million pounds ($82.8 million) to the reported first-half turnover figure this year.

Sales in the second quarter rose to 93.3 million pounds ($147.4 million) from 75.5 million pounds ($119.2 million) in the first three months, before insurance receipts of 28.9 million pounds ($45.6 million) in the first quarter and 23.5 million pounds ($37.1 million) in the second.
Including the insurance receipts, Eurotunnel said the first-half total of 221.2 million pounds ($349.4 million) was in line with upper forecasts in its debt restructuring prospectus.
Eurotunnel's freight truck service was closed for seven months following last year's blaze, which broke out on one of the open-sided truck wagons, only reopening to commercial traffic on June 15.
